literature.headline_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期基孔肯雅病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 来自 TikTok 中国的视频显示出较高的 JAMA 基准分数,而来自 Bilibili 的视频则获得了相对较高的 mDISCERN 分数。亚组分析表明,不同上传者类别的参与度指标没有统计差异,但质量得分却存在显着差异。此外,参与度指标与视频质量或可靠性的相关性较弱。 [10.3791/71918]
分析显示,测试样本中存在杂合形式 (VG) 的 V1016G 突变。没有检测到纯合突变体(GG)。生物测定结果显示这些人群对拟除虫菊酯的敏感性降低,支持了分子发现。 [10.1007/s11686-026-01424-9]
雄性比雌性化蛹早,在没有交配的情况下,雌性比雄性寿命更长。交配后,两性的寿命都会下降。形态测量参数与成人体型密切相关,表明它们的预测价值。 [10.1111/mve.70126]
国内材料(41.9%)、盆(29.4%)和花盆(28.6%)的阳性率最高,而水壶和兽皮很少被定植。值得注意的是,虽然频率较低,但赤陶罐、桶、轮胎和杂项容器产生了 70% 以上的幼虫,将它们确定为主要生产地。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10921365/v1]
隐孢子虫的血清阳性率最高(52.8%),其次是登革热(30.9%)、基孔肯雅热(25.3%)、贾第鞭毛虫(13.5%)和疟原虫(间日疟原虫11.1%;恶性疟原虫5.0%)。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-9261737/v1]

literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Videos from TikTok China showed higher JAMA benchmark scores, whereas videos from Bilibili achieved comparatively higher mDISCERN scores. Subgroup analyses indicated no statistical differences in engagement metrics across uploader categories, whereas quality scores differed significantly. [10.3791/71918]
Trends in rates of chikungunya among travelers returning to mainland France from La Réunion and Mayotte closely mirrored the sharp and compact epidemic curves observed locally. [10.1093/jtm/taag095]

The analysis revealed the presence of the V1016G mutation in heterozygous form (VG) among the tested samples. No homozygous mutants (GG) were detected. Bioassay results showed reduced susceptibility to pyrethroids in these populations, supporting the molecular findings. [10.1007/s11686-026-01424-9]

Males pupated earlier than females, and females lived longer than males in the absence of mating. After mating, longevity declined for both sexes. Morphometric parameters strongly correlated with adult size, indicating their predictive value. [10.1111/mve.70126]
Domestic materials (41.9%), basins (29.4%) and flower pots (28.6%) showed the highest positivity rates, whereas kettles and animal skins were rarely colonized. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10921365/v1]

news.lead_zh: 本期基孔肯雅病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 本文讨论了 基孔肯雅病毒 病的临床症状和体征,包括发热、多关节痛、关节症状、皮疹和其他表现。它还提到了 诊断 与登革热、寨卡病毒和其他病毒(N4、N12、N17、N18、N20、N21、N22、N23、N24、N25、N26、N27、N28、N29、N30、N31)的区别。 [news-fae369da68d70bcf]
泛美卫生组织 (PAHO) 呼吁在美洲登革热和基孔肯雅热病例增加的情况下加强 监测 和准备工作。 [news-4bd2f3e576dd40ac]
洪都拉斯卫生部确认了八例经实验室确诊的基孔肯雅热病例,其中包括阿劳卡州埃尔佩德雷加利托的本地传播群。首例输入病例是一名从尼加拉瓜马那瓜回国的31岁卡车司机。该部报告了该国当地的 传播,在边境村庄的家庭中发现了症状。 [news-18568b3bcd957cd9]
一项系统评价发现,埃博拉病毒病和基孔肯雅热的幸存者在急性感染后经常会出现持续数周至数年的持续症状。该评论发表在《BMC 传染病》杂志上。 [news-0514bd779b67d4c5]

papers.title: Imported chikungunya in French travelers returning from outbreak-affected regions.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Outbreaks of chikungunya disease are unpredictable, typically episodic, and explosive. In 2025, several such outbreaks were observed and a marked increase in imported cases of chikungunya to mainland France was reported. This study aimed to describe the rate of chikungunya in French travelers returning from La Réunion, Mayotte, Mauritius, Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Cuba, all of which showed major chikungunya resurgences in 2025, and to assess the potential burden that CHIKV outbreaks—whether officially notified or not—can cause to travelers. Methods Publicly available data from Santé Publique France were used to extract the number of chikungunya cases, and International Air Transport Association data were used for information on the number of flight tickets to estimate traveler numbers. These data were used to derive monthly rates of imported cases of chikungunya to mainland France from January to December 2025. Results Trends in rates of chikungunya among travelers returning to mainland France from La Réunion and Mayotte closely mirrored the sharp and compact epidemic curves observed locally. Peak imported rates exceeded 1,800 cases/100,000 travelers (La Réunion [April]) and 400 cases/100,000 travelers (Mayotte [May]) and remained above 100 cases/100,000 travelers for March, April, May, and June (La Réunion) and April, May, and June (Mayotte). For Mauritius, Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Cuba, estimated peak rates were 248, 338, 90, and 2,480 cases/100,000 travelers, respectively, although it was noted that some outbreaks were not officially notified or were reported late. Conclusions Returning travelers to mainland France from regions facing a chikungunya outbreak in 2025 showed a substantial burden of infection and gave rise to local spread of disease, highlighting the importance of robust surveillance systems and timely outbreak notification.

This study aimed to describe the rate of chikungunya in French travelers returning from La Réunion, Mayotte, Mauritius, Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Cuba, all of which showed major chikungunya resurgences in 2025, and to assess the potential burden that CHIKV outbreaks-whether officially notified or not-can cause to travelers. METHODS Publicly available data from Santé Publique France were used to extract the number of chikungunya cases, and International Air Transport Association data were used for information on the number of flight tickets to estimate traveler numbers. These data were used to derive monthly rates of imported cases of chikungunya to mainland France from January to December 2025. RESULTS Trends in rates of chikungunya among travelers returning to mainland France from La Réunion and Mayotte closely mirrored the sharp and compact epidemic curves observed locally. Peak imported rates exceeded 1,800 cases/100,000 travelers (La Réunion [April]) and 400 cases/100,000 travelers (Mayotte [May]) and remained above 100 cases/100,000 travelers for March, April, May, and June (La Réunion) and April, May, and June (Mayotte). For Mauritius, Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Cuba, estimated peak rates were 248, 338, 90, and 2,480 cases/100,000 travelers, respectively, although it was noted that some outbreaks were not officially notified or were reported late. CONCLUSIONS Returning travelers to mainland France from regions facing a chikungunya outbreak in 2025 showed a substantial burden of infection and gave rise to local spread of disease, highlighting the importance of robust surveillance systems and timely outbreak notification.

papers.title: Content and Quality Analysis of Chikungunya Fever-Related Online Information on Social Media: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: An outbreak of chikungunya fever (CHIKF) occurred in China in 2025. The rapid increase in new cases has drawn the attention of health authorities. The outbreak also sparked widespread discussion on social media platforms. Fear-inducing and uncertain information about CHIKF circulated rapidly online, which may complicate risk communication and outbreak management efforts. In this study, we assessed the content characteristics, video quality, information reliability, transparency, and engagement of CHIKF-related short videos across the two platforms. We searched TikTok China and Bilibili using the term "chikungunya fever" and included the top 100 videos from each platform on October 9, 2025 (N = 200). Video quality was assessed using the Global Quality Scale (GQS) and the Video Information and Quality Index (VIQI); information reliability was evaluated using the modified DISCERN (mDISCERN); transparency was measured using the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark criteria; and engagement was quantified using platform-based interaction metrics. Statistical analyses were performed to compare video characteristics across platforms and uploader categories, and to evaluate associations between these characteristics and quality scores. Videos from TikTok China showed higher JAMA benchmark scores, whereas videos from Bilibili achieved comparatively higher mDISCERN scores. Subgroup analyses indicated no statistical differences in engagement metrics across uploader categories, whereas quality scores differed significantly. In addition, engagement metrics showed weak correlations with video quality or reliability. The quality and reliability scores for CHIKF-related short videos on the two platforms were relatively low. The results support careful consideration of whether video quality and information reliability should be more explicitly incorporated into platform governance and content distribution strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 2025年中国发生了一场基孔肯雅热(CHIKF)的暴发,新增病例的快速增加引起了卫生当局的关注。暴发 还在社交媒体平台上引发了广泛讨论,有关 CHIKF 的令人恐惧和不确定的信息在网上迅速传播,这可能会使风险沟通和 暴发 管理工作复杂化。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们使用“基孔肯雅热”搜索了 TikTok 中国和 Bilibili,并收录了 2025 年 10 月 9 日每个平台排名前 100 的视频(N = 200)。
elements_zh.methods: 使用全球质量量表(GQS)和视频信息和质量指数(VIQI)评估视频质量;使用修改后的DISCERN(mDISCERN)评估信息可靠性;使用美国医学会杂志 (JAMA) 基准标准衡量透明度;使用基于平台的交互指标来量化参与度。
elements_zh.main_results: 来自 TikTok 中国的视频显示出较高的 JAMA 基准分数,而来自 Bilibili 的视频则获得了相对较高的 mDISCERN 分数。亚组分析表明,不同上传者类别的参与度指标没有统计差异,但质量得分却存在显着差异。此外,参与度指标与视频质量或可靠性的相关性较弱。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 两个平台上CHIKF相关短视频的质量和可靠性评分均较低。结果支持仔细考虑视频质量和信息可靠性是否应该更明确地纳入平台治理和内容分发策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 调查结果强调需要改进社交媒体平台的内容治理,以确保向公众传播有关 基孔肯雅热 的准确可靠的信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其横截面设计和选择热门视频时可能存在的偏见而受到限制。证据是温和的,因为它基于观察数据和基于平台的指标。

papers.title: Nanopore Sequencing for Chikungunya Virus: Principles and Application.
papers.abstract: Nanopore sequencing is transforming viral genomics through real-time, portable, long-read analysis of RNA and DNA. Unlike traditional short-read platforms, it detects nucleotide sequences by measuring ionic current changes as nucleic acids pass through nanoscale pores, enabling direct single-molecule sequencing and base modification detection. Its simplicity, flexibility, and capacity for ultra-long reads make it ideal for resolving complex genomic regions, structural variants, and full viral genomes. These advantages have accelerated its use in pathogen surveillance and outbreak response, especially in resource-limited settings. For chikungunya virus (CHIKV), nanopore sequencing allows rapid, culture-independent recovery of complete genomes from clinical and vector samples, enabling real-time tracking of viral diversity, evolution, and spread. Experiences from Ebola, Zika, and COVID-19 have demonstrated the power of portable sequencing, now applied to CHIKV monitoring. Advances in tools such as Guppy, Dorado, Minimap2, and Medaka enhance read quality, consensus accuracy, and downstream analyses. Despite challenges in basecalling and error correction, robust quality control pipelines ensure reliable results. Ongoing improvements in chemistry, flow cell design, and machine learning will further enhance fidelity and throughput, establishing nanopore sequencing as a cornerstone of CHIKV genomic surveillance and epidemic preparedness.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为基孔肯雅病毒的更有效监测策略的制定提供依据,从而增强疫情响应和疫情应对能力。

papers.abstract_zh: 纳米孔测序通过对 RNA 和 DNA 进行实时、便携式、长读长分析,正在改变病毒基因组学。与传统的短读长平台不同,它通过测量核酸通过纳米级孔时离子电流的变化来检测核苷酸序列,从而实现直接单分子测序和碱基修饰检测。其简单性、灵活性和超长读取能力使其成为解析复杂基因组区域、结构变异和完整病毒 基因组 的理想选择。这些优点加速了其在病原体 监测 和 暴发 响应中的使用,特别是在资源有限的环境中。对于 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV),纳米孔测序可以从临床和 媒介 样本中快速、独立于培养物恢复完整的 基因组,从而实现病毒多样性、进化 和传播的实时跟踪。埃博拉、寨卡和 COVID-19 的经验证明了便携式测序的强大功能,现已应用于 CHIKV 监测。Guppy、Dorado、Minimap2 和 Medaka 等工具的进步提高了读取质量、共识准确性和下游分析。尽管碱基识别和纠错方面存在挑战,但强大的质量控制流程可确保可靠的结果。化学、流动池设计和机器学习方面的持续改进将进一步提高保真度和通量,将纳米孔测序确立为 CHIKV 基因组监测 和流行病防范的基石。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨纳米孔测序在基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)基因组学中的应用,以应对在疫情期间快速、便携和准确追踪病毒多样性及传播的迫切需求。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究聚焦于纳米孔测序在基孔肯雅病毒中的原理与应用,考察其在临床和环境样本中用于恢复完整病毒基因组和监测病毒传播的使用情况。
analysis_zh.methods: 纳米孔测序通过测量核酸穿过纳米级孔时的离子电流变化,直接对RNA和DNA进行测序,从而实现对基孔肯雅病毒基因组的实时、单分子分析,无需依赖培养。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该方法展示了从临床和环境样本中快速恢复完整病毒基因组的能力,有助于在疫情期间实时追踪病毒多样性、传播及扩散。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为病原体监测领域的重要进展,特别是在资源有限的环境中,纳米孔测序提供了一种灵活且强大的工具,用于基孔肯雅病毒的监测。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为基孔肯雅病毒的更有效监测策略的制定提供依据,从而增强疫情响应和疫情应对能力。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究承认在碱基调用和错误校正方面存在挑战,但强调了稳健的质量控制流程,确保了可靠的结果,支持了中等程度的证据可信度。

papers.title: Overview of Chikungunya Virus Epidemiology, Biology, and Pathogenesis.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, is transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The virus causes an acute febrile illness characterized by severe, often bilateral polyarthralgia, with potential progression to chronic musculoskeletal pain and rare systemic complications involving cardiovascular and neurological systems. CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane. Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination; VLP-based vaccines (e.g., Vimkunya) show promise, while live-attenuated formulations face safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist; current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development.

papers.title_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)概述、生物学及系统发育
papers.source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, is transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The virus causes an acute febrile illness characterized by severe, often bilateral polyarthralgia, with potential progression to chronic musculoskeletal pain and rare systemic complications involving cardiovascular and neurological systems. CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane. Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination; VLP-based vaccines (e.g., Vimkunya) show promise, while live-attenuated formulations face safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist; current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development.
papers.abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV),一种属于Togaviridae科的虫媒α病毒,主要通过埃及伊蚊(Aedes aegypti)和白纹伊蚊(Aedes albopictus)传播。该病毒引起一种急性发热性疾病,特征为严重的、常为双侧性关节痛,可能进展为慢性肌肉骨骼疼痛,并偶有涉及心血管和神经系统系统的全身并发症。CHIKV具有球形、包膜的病毒颗粒(约70 nm),呈T = 4二十面体对称结构,包含介导受体结合和膜融合的E1/E2糖蛋白异二聚体。其正链RNA基因组(约11.8 kb)编码用于复制的非结构蛋白和用于病毒颗粒组装的结构蛋白。病毒复制发生在细胞质囊泡中,涉及基因组和亚基因组RNA的合成,随后是糖蛋白成熟和在细胞膜上出芽。从流行病学角度看,CHIKV已扩展至非洲和亚洲以外的地区,其主要传播模式由适应性进化增强其传播能力。自2013年引入美洲以来,全球发病率仍保持较高水平,2025年报告了超过180,000例确诊病例。预防策略依赖于媒介控制和疫苗接种;基于病毒样颗粒(VLP)的疫苗(如Vimkunya)显示出前景,而减毒活疫苗则面临安全性问题。目前尚无获批的抗病毒药物;现有管理措施为支持性治疗,但针对病毒复制和免疫调节的试验性疗法正在研发中。

papers.title: Protocol for Detecting and Sequencing Chikungunya Virus from Field-Collected Mosquitoes.
papers.abstract: Arboviral diseases represent a major public health challenge, especially in tropical regions where environmental conditions may favor the proliferation and spread of mosquito vectors. Thus, early and accurate detection of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in mosquito populations can be a valuable tool for effective surveillance of circulating variants and for identifying new viral introductions. Given the challenges of detecting arboviruses in field-captured mosquitoes, we describe an integrated workflow for CHIKV molecular detection and whole-genome sequencing. This protocol includes mosquito homogenization using a bead-based mechanical disruptor, RNA extraction using TRIzol reagent with minor modifications, molecular screening using CHIKV-specific RT-qPCR, and whole-genome amplification followed by sequencing on Illumina platforms. Despite the protocol being optimized for individual mosquitoes, it results in high-quality RNA suitable for both entomological surveillance and genomic analysis. As this protocol allows recovery of complete CHIKV genomes from mosquito specimens, it can serve as a basis for genomic epidemiology studies, enabling monitoring of viral diversity and lineage dynamics, and facilitating early detection of emerging variants to support timely and targeted public health interventions in endemic and at-risk regions.

papers.title: Global patterns of genetic diversity and evolution in chikungunya virus E2 glycoprotein
papers.abstract: The E2 glycoprotein of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) mediates host-cell attachment and entry and contains key antigenic determinants targeted by host immune responses. Variation in E2 can influence host interaction, immune recognition, lineage diversification, and epidemic fitness, it represents a biologically relevant target for assessing evolutionary pressures and epidemic dynamics. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of E2 genetic diversity using a dataset of sequences collected across regions, hosts, and epidemic periods. Diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotypes network analysis were applied to characterize evolutionary pressures acting on E2 glycoprotein. To assess the influence of geography, host, and time on viral population structure, we performed spatial–temporal stratification and analysis to assess clustering patterns across lineages and regions using Fixation index test (Fst). Nucleotide diversity varied considerably across time, with the pre-expansion period (pre-2004) showing the highest diversity (Pi = 0.085), while more recent outbreak periods exhibited comparatively reduced diversity (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests revealed signatures of both purifying and positive selection across the three CKIKV E2 lineages (negatively statistically significant Tajima D, Fu and Li’s D, and Fu and Li’s F tests, p -values < 0.05) supported by codon‐based analyses showing pervasive purifying constraint across the E2 gene but recurrent diversifying signals at lineage‐specific sites, notably codon 146 in the West African lineage, codons 220, 245, 247, and 254 in the Asian lineage, and codons 54, 56, 102, 145, 163, 177, and 350 in the East/Central/South/African lineage. Population structure analyses using Fst indicated significant genetic differentiation between regional populations, reflecting restricted gene flow and localized evolutionary trajectories. Haplotype network analysis highlighted distinct clustering patterns shaped by geography and epidemic waves, reflecting the persistence of lineage-specific signatures across regions. At the same time, reduced connectivity among recent outbreak strains point to more discrete intercontinental movement events, likely driven by human-mediated vector dispersal or travel-associated introductions. Collectively, these findings underscore the spatiotemporal evolution of CHIKV E2 glycoprotein and its implications for viral adaptation and immune evasion.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the genetic diversity and evolution of the E2 glycoprotein in chikungunya virus (CHIKV), focusing on its role in host-cell attachment, immune recognition, and lineage diversification.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed a dataset of CHIKV sequences collected across different regions, hosts, and epidemic periods to characterize evolutionary pressures on the E2 glycoprotein.
analysis.methods: The researchers used diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotype network analysis to assess genetic variation and evolutionary dynamics, and performed spatial–temporal stratification and Fixation index (Fst) analysis to evaluate population structure.
analysis.main_results: Nucleotide diversity was highest in the pre-expansion period (Pi = 0.085) and decreased in more recent outbreak periods (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests showed signs of both purifying and positive selection across lineages, with specific codons identified as sites of diversifying signals.

papers.title_zh: 全球遗传多样性及进化在基孔肯雅病毒 E2糖蛋白中的模式
papers.source_body_en: The E2 glycoprotein of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) mediates host-cell attachment and entry and contains key antigenic determinants targeted by host immune responses. Variation in E2 can influence host interaction, immune recognition, lineage diversification, and epidemic fitness, it represents a biologically relevant target for assessing evolutionary pressures and epidemic dynamics. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of E2 genetic diversity using a dataset of sequences collected across regions, hosts, and epidemic periods. Diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotypes network analysis were applied to characterize evolutionary pressures acting on E2 glycoprotein. To assess the influence of geography, host, and time on viral population structure, we performed spatial–temporal stratification and analysis to assess clustering patterns across lineages and regions using Fixation index test (Fst). Nucleotide diversity varied considerably across time, with the pre-expansion period (pre-2004) showing the highest diversity (Pi = 0.085), while more recent outbreak periods exhibited comparatively reduced diversity (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests revealed signatures of both purifying and positive selection across the three CKIKV E2 lineages (negatively statistically significant Tajima D, Fu and Li’s D, and Fu and Li’s F tests, p -values < 0.05) supported by codon‐based analyses showing pervasive purifying constraint across the E2 gene but recurrent diversifying signals at lineage‐specific sites, notably codon 146 in the West African lineage, codons 220, 245, 247, and 254 in the Asian lineage, and codons 54, 56, 102, 145, 163, 177, and 350 in the East/Central/South/African lineage. Population structure analyses using Fst indicated significant genetic differentiation between regional populations, reflecting restricted gene flow and localized evolutionary trajectories. Haplotype network analysis highlighted distinct clustering patterns shaped by geography and epidemic waves, reflecting the persistence of lineage-specific signatures across regions. At the same time, reduced connectivity among recent outbreak strains point to more discrete intercontinental movement events, likely driven by human-mediated vector dispersal or travel-associated introductions. Collectively, these findings underscore the spatiotemporal evolution of CHIKV E2 glycoprotein and its implications for viral adaptation and immune evasion.

papers.title: Workflow for Long-Read Amplicon Sequencing of Chikungunya Virus Using Oxford Nanopore Technology.
papers.abstract: This protocol provides a comprehensive, step-by-step workflow for whole-genome sequencing of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) using an amplicon-based strategy optimized for Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) platforms. The procedure includes detailed instructions for sample handling, viral RNA extraction, quality control, cDNA synthesis, multiplex PCR amplification, library preparation, sequencing, and primary bioinformatic processing. The protocol is designed to maximize reproducibility across laboratories and is suitable for genomic surveillance applications, including outbreak investigation and molecular epidemiology, even when working with low-to-moderate viral loads.

papers.title: Optimized Amplicon Strategy for Long-Read Sequencing of the Chikungunya Virus Genome.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense RNA alphavirus transmitted to humans primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. Its global circulation and significant public health impact underscore the need to better understand the molecular mechanisms driving CHIKV pathogenesis and transmission. Although robust molecular biology methods exist for CHIKV genome sequencing, a major limitation for surveillance and research is the inability to determine whether two nucleotide variations co-occur within the same viral genome when they are separated beyond the span of typical short-read designs. Here, we describe an optimized approach for processing CHIKV RNA samples that generates large amplicons suitable for long-read nanopore sequencing. This protocol enables amplification of the complete CHIKV genome in only two or three amplicons and facilitates detection of co-occurring nucleotide variations across 4-7.5 kb within the same molecule, thereby simplifying sequencing workflows and improving resolution in studies of viral evolution.

papers.title_zh: 用于 基孔肯雅病毒 基因组 长读长测序的优化扩增子策略。
papers.source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense RNA alphavirus transmitted to humans primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. Its global circulation and significant public health impact underscore the need to better understand the molecular mechanisms driving CHIKV pathogenesis and transmission. Although robust molecular biology methods exist for CHIKV genome sequencing, a major limitation for surveillance and research is the inability to determine whether two nucleotide variations co-occur within the same viral genome when they are separated beyond the span of typical short-read designs. Here, we describe an optimized approach for processing CHIKV RNA samples that generates large amplicons suitable for long-read nanopore sequencing. This protocol enables amplification of the complete CHIKV genome in only two or three amplicons and facilitates detection of co-occurring nucleotide variations across 4-7.5 kb within the same molecule, thereby simplifying sequencing workflows and improving resolution in studies of viral evolution.

papers.title: Assessing the Vector Competence for Chikungunya Virus in Mosquitoes.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a human pathogenic, mosquito-borne virus (arbovirus), which is causing epidemic outbreaks among human populations in Africa, Asia, Europe, and South- and Central America including the Caribbean. The development of novel approaches to prevent mosquito transmission of the virus in the field requires a detailed study of CHIKV interactions with its mosquito vectors in the laboratory. In this chapter, we describe how to prepare Aedes aegypti mosquitoes for the infection with freshly cultivated CHIKV. We also describe quantitative and qualitative viral detection assays in mosquitoes based on plaque assays and the amplification of saliva samples in cell culture.

papers.source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a human pathogenic, mosquito-borne virus (arbovirus), which is causing epidemic outbreaks among human populations in Africa, Asia, Europe, and South- and Central America including the Caribbean. The development of novel approaches to prevent mosquito transmission of the virus in the field requires a detailed study of CHIKV interactions with its mosquito vectors in the laboratory. In this chapter, we describe how to prepare Aedes aegypti mosquitoes for the infection with freshly cultivated CHIKV. We also describe quantitative and qualitative viral detection assays in mosquitoes based on plaque assays and the amplification of saliva samples in cell culture.

papers.title: Plaque Reduction Neutralization Test Against Chikungunya Virus Using Liver Homogenate.
papers.abstract: We adapted the plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) to detect chikungunya virus (CHIKV) neutralizing antibodies in liver homogenates instead of serum. This approach enables serological investigation using tissues collected from animal carcasses as nonhuman primate ones, during arbovirus surveillance, expanding opportunities for CHIKV monitoring and strengthening epidemiological surveillance efforts.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The research involved adapting the plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) to use liver homogenates instead of serum, focusing on nonhuman primate tissues collected during arbovirus surveillance.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces an adaptation of the plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) to detect chikungunya virus (CHIKV) neutralizing antibodies in liver homogenates rather than serum. The research was motivated by the need for alternative serological methods in arbovirus surveillance, particularly when serum samples are unavailable. The modified PRNT successfully identified CHIKV neutralizing antibodies in nonhuman primate tissues, offering a new approach for CHIKV monitoring. This method could enhance epidemiological surveillance efforts by utilizing tissues from animal carcasses. However, the study lacks statistical analysis and broader validation, limiting the confidence in its application. The findings are significant for improving surveillance strategies but require further testing to establish their reliability in diverse contexts.

papers.title: Surface Plasmon Resonance-Based Analysis of Ligand Binding Kinetics in Chikungunya Virus Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging arbovirus lacking widely effective antiviral therapies, highlighting the need to characterize molecular interactions essential for its replication and pathogenesis. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a sensitive, label-free technique that enables real-time analysis of biomolecular interactions by detecting refractive index changes at a sensor surface. SPR provides precise kinetic and affinity measurements for protein-protein, protein-RNA, and protein-ligand interactions using minimal sample quantities and supporting high-throughput screening. In CHIKV research, it has been applied to evaluate antiviral compounds, antibodies, receptor binding, and viral protein complexes. This chapter outlines key methodological considerations, including ligand preparation, immobilization strategies, assay optimization, and kinetic analysis.

papers.source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging arbovirus lacking widely effective antiviral therapies, highlighting the need to characterize molecular interactions essential for its replication and pathogenesis. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a sensitive, label-free technique that enables real-time analysis of biomolecular interactions by detecting refractive index changes at a sensor surface. SPR provides precise kinetic and affinity measurements for protein-protein, protein-RNA, and protein-ligand interactions using minimal sample quantities and supporting high-throughput screening. In CHIKV research, it has been applied to evaluate antiviral compounds, antibodies, receptor binding, and viral protein complexes. This chapter outlines key methodological considerations, including ligand preparation, immobilization strategies, assay optimization, and kinetic analysis.

papers.title: RT-RPA-Assisted CRISPR/Cas12a-Based Isothermal Detection of Chikungunya Virus.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is transmitted through the bite of Aedes mosquitoes, specifically A. CHIKV belongs to the alphavirus with a positive-sense ssRNA genome of 11-12 kb size. The virus has been reported from various geographical regions across the globe. Chikungunya fever is an acute febrile illness, which, if left untreated, may develop into chronic arthralgia that may persist for several months or acute encephalitis syndrome. Therefore, early diagnosis of CHIKV is crucial to initiate prompt supportive treatment. Laboratory diagnosis of CHIKV typically relies on serological tests such as IgM antigen capture ELISA and molecular methods including RT-PCR or qRT-PCR. However, both these methods are not viable in peripheral settings. This chapter highlights recent advancements in molecular detection techniques for CHIKV, specifically isothermal detection methods that eliminate the requirement for complex instruments. The detection is facilitated by RT-RPA and CRISPR/Cas12a endonuclease. The assay offers advantages over existing methods such as rapid and early detection, and eliminates cross-over contamination, ultra-sensitivity, high specificity, and ease of result interpretation.

papers.source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is transmitted through the bite of Aedes mosquitoes, specifically A. CHIKV belongs to the alphavirus with a positive-sense ssRNA genome of 11-12 kb size. The virus has been reported from various geographical regions across the globe. Chikungunya fever is an acute febrile illness, which, if left untreated, may develop into chronic arthralgia that may persist for several months or acute encephalitis syndrome. Therefore, early diagnosis of CHIKV is crucial to initiate prompt supportive treatment. Laboratory diagnosis of CHIKV typically relies on serological tests such as IgM antigen capture ELISA and molecular methods including RT-PCR or qRT-PCR. However, both these methods are not viable in peripheral settings. This chapter highlights recent advancements in molecular detection techniques for CHIKV, specifically isothermal detection methods that eliminate the requirement for complex instruments. The detection is facilitated by RT-RPA and CRISPR/Cas12a endonuclease. The assay offers advantages over existing methods such as rapid and early detection, and eliminates cross-over contamination, ultra-sensitivity, high specificity, and ease of result interpretation.

papers.title: Production of Viral Particles from a Chikungunya Virus Infectious Clone.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus, which poses challenges for its study and genetic manipulation. Because direct mutagenesis of viral RNA genomes is technically impractical, reverse genetics systems are essential tools for investigating viral biology. To enable such approaches, infectious clones containing a full-length cDNA copy of the viral genome are constructed. The cDNA is positioned under the control of a bacteriophage RNA polymerase promoter, allowing commercial RNA polymerases to use the linearized plasmid as a template for the in vitro transcription of full-length viral genomic RNA (gRNA). Importantly, positive-sense viral genomes serve as mRNAs for the translation of viral proteins in a cellular environment, meaning that these transcripts contain all the information required to initiate viral replication. Following transfection into permissive cultured cells, viral proteins are expressed, enabling genome replication and, ultimately, the recovery of infectious particles from the cell supernatant. Here, we describe a detailed procedure for generating CHIKV particles through plasmid linearization, in vitro transcription, and subsequent RNA transfection.

papers.title: Naked-Eye Visual Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Method for the Rapid Detection of Chikungunya Virus.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) represents a significant global health threat due to its recent resurgence. This protocol highlights the use of capillary-modified visual loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) technology for the rapid detection of CHIKV. We employed Vero cells for virus propagation and utilized the MolPure Viral DNA/RNA Kit for nucleic acid extraction, successfully amplifying extracted viral RNA at 63°C for 25 min. The presence of CHIKV was indicated by a distinct yellowish-green color change, demonstrating the effectiveness and simplicity of this protocol. Our protocol underscores the potential of LAMP technology as a rapid diagnostic tool for CHIKV, enabling timely public health interventions.

analysis.summary_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) poses a growing global health threat, prompting the development of a rapid detection method. Researchers established an in vitro protocol using Vero cells to propagate CHIKV, extracted viral RNA with the MolPure kit, and performed loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) at 63 °C for 25 minutes. Detection relied on a distinct yellowish-green color change, confirming CHIKV presence and demonstrating the assay’s simplicity and effectiveness. The authors interpret this as a promising rapid diagnostic tool that could enable timely public health interventions. By offering a point-of-care, visual LAMP assay, the protocol has the potential to enhance CHIKV surveillance and outbreak response, especially in resource-limited settings. No limitations or evidence strength assessments were reported in the abstract.

papers.title: In Silico Drug Design of Chikungunya Antivirals: Using Consensus Methods for Virtual Screening.
papers.abstract: Structure-based virtual screening is an attractive strategy in drug design. It enables the selection of potential binders to target biomolecules with known molecular structures, providing a rational framework for studying their mechanisms of action and guiding further optimization. However, accurately predicting the free energy of binding remains an extremely challenging task, and the available tools only provide approximate estimates. In this context, one strategy to improve the predictive power of virtual screening and increase the probability of identifying true binders is to employ multiple docking algorithms and combine their results using a consensus method. In this chapter, we will describe a step-by-step methodology to perform this task. We will conduct a virtual screening using AutoDock Vina, AutoDock4, and LeDock, and then combine their results employing the Exponential Consensus Ranking algorithm. Finally, we will discuss possible extensions of this strategy, such as incorporating Molecular Dynamics simulations as an additional filter in the virtual screening or integrating the novel Artificial Intelligence-based methodologies into the consensus framework.

papers.title_zh: 基孔肯雅热 抗病毒药物 的计算机药物设计:使用共识方法进行虚拟筛选。
papers.source_body_en: Structure-based virtual screening is an attractive strategy in drug design. It enables the selection of potential binders to target biomolecules with known molecular structures, providing a rational framework for studying their mechanisms of action and guiding further optimization. However, accurately predicting the free energy of binding remains an extremely challenging task, and the available tools only provide approximate estimates. In this context, one strategy to improve the predictive power of virtual screening and increase the probability of identifying true binders is to employ multiple docking algorithms and combine their results using a consensus method. In this chapter, we will describe a step-by-step methodology to perform this task. We will conduct a virtual screening using AutoDock Vina, AutoDock4, and LeDock, and then combine their results employing the Exponential Consensus Ranking algorithm. Finally, we will discuss possible extensions of this strategy, such as incorporating Molecular Dynamics simulations as an additional filter in the virtual screening or integrating the novel Artificial Intelligence-based methodologies into the consensus framework.

papers.title: Expression and Purification of nsP2 Protease of Chikungunya Virus.
papers.abstract: The nonstructural protein 2 (nsP2) of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an essential cysteine protease involved in viral polyprotein processing and replication complex regulation. Biochemical and structural studies of nsP2 require the availability of highly pure and enzymatically active protein. In this chapter, we describe a straightforward protocol for the heterologous expression and purification of CHIKV nsP2 protease domain (nsP2pro) in Escherichia coli. The protein is expressed at low temperature as a His-tagged construct and purified under native conditions by immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography, followed by dialysis for buffer exchange. The procedure typically yields milligram quantities of highly pure (>95%) and active nsP2pro, and has been successfully applied to wild-type and mutant variants for enzymatic assays and inhibitor screening.

papers.title: Chikungunya Virus Infection in Paraffin-Embedded Tissue: Analysis of Histological Alterations and Viral Detection by Immunohistochemistry.
papers.abstract: Histopathological analysis of tissues infected with Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), including biopsy and autopsy specimens, can provide valuable insights into the pathogenesis of atypical and fatal cases. By examining tissue architecture and cellular alterations under the microscope, it is possible to identify patterns of injury, inflammation, and cellular degeneration. These morphological findings provide evidence of how the pathogen interacts with host cells and tissues. Moreover, immunohistochemistry may be performed in tissue sections for the detection of viral antigens. Importantly, this technique allows the characterization of diverse biologically relevant targets in tissue samples, such as distinct immune cell subsets, cytokines, and additional molecular markers. This is accomplished by the use of antibodies selected for their specificity toward the antigen of interest. In this chapter, we present a concise overview of how histological analysis and immunohistochemical approaches can enhance the understanding of CHIKV-associated pathological mechanisms.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 感染组织的组织学改变和病毒检测,以更好地了解其在非典型和致命病例中的 发病机制。这对于识别与 CHIKV 感染相关的损伤、炎症和细胞变性模式非常重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 CHIKV 感染个体的活检和尸检标本的组织病理学变化,重点研究病毒如何与 宿主 细胞和组织相互作用。它包括一系列标本来捕捉不同的病理表现。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及组织结构和细胞变化的组织学分析,以及检测病毒抗原的免疫组织化学。这些技术用于表征生物相关目标,例如组织样本中的免疫细胞亚群、细胞因子和分子标记。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究观察到了受感染组织中 CHIKV 诱导的损伤、炎症和细胞变性的组织学改变。免疫组织化学证实这些样本中存在病毒抗原。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了组织学和免疫组织化学方法在阐明 CHIKV 感染病理机制方面的实用性。这为病毒与 宿主 组织的相互作用提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果可以为改进的诊断方法提供信息并增强对 CHIKV 发病机制 的理解,这对于开发有针对性的 监测 和 治疗 策略至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象级别的描述,不提供详细的统计或实验数据。由于缺乏具体的数值研究结果和综合分析,证据的强度中等。

papers.title: Assessing Chikungunya Virus Protease Activity and Pharmacological Inhibition Using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp Fluorogenic Peptide Substrate.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus, a mosquito-borne alphavirus, poses a significant global health threat due to its rapid spread and lack of approved antiviral therapies. The viral nonstructural protein 2 protease (nsP2p) plays a critical role in processing the viral polyprotein to produce key viral enzymes, making it an attractive target for drug development. In this study, we describe the expression and purification of recombinant CHIKV nsP2 protease and establish a robust fluorogenic assay to measure its enzymatic activity using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp peptide substrate. The assay enables real-time monitoring of proteolytic cleavage and provides a platform for evaluating small-molecule inhibitors. We present optimized conditions for protein expression in E. coli, affinity purification, and tag removal, achieving high-purity nsP2 protease suitable for biochemical characterization. Using this system, we also provide a robust protocol for determining IC50 values for candidate inhibitors. This work provides a reproducible methodology for high-throughput screening of CHIKV protease inhibitors, facilitating the discovery of potential antiviral compounds against chikungunya virus.

papers.title_zh: 使用 acc-CHIK 15 -dnp 荧光肽底物评估 基孔肯雅病毒 蛋白酶活性和药理抑制。
papers.source_body_en: Chikungunya virus, a mosquito-borne alphavirus, poses a significant global health threat due to its rapid spread and lack of approved antiviral therapies. The viral nonstructural protein 2 protease (nsP2p) plays a critical role in processing the viral polyprotein to produce key viral enzymes, making it an attractive target for drug development. In this study, we describe the expression and purification of recombinant CHIKV nsP2 protease and establish a robust fluorogenic assay to measure its enzymatic activity using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp peptide substrate. The assay enables real-time monitoring of proteolytic cleavage and provides a platform for evaluating small-molecule inhibitors. We present optimized conditions for protein expression in E. coli, affinity purification, and tag removal, achieving high-purity nsP2 protease suitable for biochemical characterization. Using this system, we also provide a robust protocol for determining IC50 values for candidate inhibitors. This work provides a reproducible methodology for high-throughput screening of CHIKV protease inhibitors, facilitating the discovery of potential antiviral compounds against chikungunya virus.
papers.abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒 是一种蚊媒甲病毒,由于其快速传播且缺乏经批准的 抗病毒药物 疗法,对全球健康构成重大威胁。病毒非结构蛋白 2 蛋白酶 (nsP2p) 在加工病毒多蛋白以产生关键病毒酶方面发挥着关键作用,使其成为药物开发的有吸引力的目标。在本研究中,我们描述了重组 CHIKV nsP2 蛋白酶的表达和纯化,并建立了强大的荧光测定法,使用 acc-CHIK 15 -dnp 肽底物测量其酶活性。该测定能够实时监测蛋白水解裂解,并提供评估小分子抑制剂的平台。我们提出了大肠杆菌中蛋白质表达、亲和纯化和标签去除的优化条件,从而获得适合生化表征的高纯度 nsP2 蛋白酶。使用该系统,我们还提供了一个强大的方案来确定候选抑制剂的 IC50 值。这项工作为 CHIKV 蛋白酶抑制剂的高通量筛选提供了一种可重复的方法,有助于发现针对 基孔肯雅病毒 的潜在 抗病毒药物 化合物。

papers.title: Quantification of Chikungunya Virus RNA by Real-Time RT-PCR Assay.
papers.abstract: RT-qPCR is characterized by‌ high sensitivity, strong specificity, excellent reproducibility, and operational simplicity, ‌enabling‌ rapid quantification of viral RNA within a short timeframe. The real-time PCR system relies upon the measurement of a fluorescent reporter during PCR, in which the amount of emitted fluorescence is directly proportional to the amount of the PCR product in a reaction. Here, we describe the use of TaqMan® probe-based one-tube Real-time reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) for the detection and quantification of the Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) RNA.

papers.title: Determination of Chikungunya Virus Infectious Titer Using Plaque Assays.
papers.abstract: The plaque-forming assay is the gold-standard method for measuring infectious viral particles. In this technique, lytic viruses infect and destroy host cells, but their spread is restricted by a viscous overlay medium. As a result, new viral particles can only infect neighboring cells, leading to localized clear areas known as plaques, which become visible after staining the remaining living cells. The number of plaques reflects the number of infectious viral particles initially present in the sample and is reported as plaque-forming units (PFU) per sample volume. In this protocol, we describe step by step how to perform a plaque-forming assay to determine the concentration of chikungunya virus in a cell culture supernatant.

papers.title: Automated Counting of Chikungunya Virus-Formed Plaques.
papers.abstract: The cytopathic effect (CPE) is a key to understanding the pathogenicity of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and is useful for evaluating viral infectivity in vitro. The plaque assay, based on the CPE induced by viral infection, provides an infectious virus titer for test samples. Additionally, the assay is simple, quantitative, and cost-effective. Thus, the plaque assay remains the gold standard for determining the infectivity of CHIKV. However, manually counting of virus-induced plaques with the naked eye or under the microscope is often time-consuming and labor-intensive. Therefore, automated plaque-counting software would improve the consistency and efficiency of plaque counting. We recently developed plaQuest, a stand-alone Windows software that enables rapid, reliable plaque counting for CHIKV. In this chapter, we describe the basic procedure for detecting and counting the CHIKV-formed plaques in a 24-well plate.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of evaluating the pathogenicity of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) through the cytopathic effect (CPE), which is crucial for understanding viral infectivity in vitro.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study describes a method for detecting and counting CHIKV-formed plaques in a 24-well plate, focusing on the procedures used for plaque assay.
elements_en.methods: The plaque assay, which is based on the cytopathic effect induced by viral infection, is used to determine the infectious virus titer for test samples. The assay is noted to be simple, quantitative, and cost-effective.
elements_en.main_results: The plaque assay remains the gold standard for determining the infectivity of CHIKV, as it provides an accurate measure of viral titer.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the plaque assay is a reliable method for assessing CHIKV infectivity, and they highlight its continued relevance as a standard technique.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the continued use of plaque assays in virology research for CHIKV, which is essential for understanding its pathogenicity and developing diagnostic tools.

papers.title_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒 形成的斑块的自动计数。
papers.source_body_en: The cytopathic effect (CPE) is a key to understanding the pathogenicity of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and is useful for evaluating viral infectivity in vitro. The plaque assay, based on the CPE induced by viral infection, provides an infectious virus titer for test samples. Additionally, the assay is simple, quantitative, and cost-effective. Thus, the plaque assay remains the gold standard for determining the infectivity of CHIKV. However, manually counting of virus-induced plaques with the naked eye or under the microscope is often time-consuming and labor-intensive. Therefore, automated plaque-counting software would improve the consistency and efficiency of plaque counting. We recently developed plaQuest, a stand-alone Windows software that enables rapid, reliable plaque counting for CHIKV. In this chapter, we describe the basic procedure for detecting and counting the CHIKV-formed plaques in a 24-well plate.
papers.abstract_zh: 细胞病变效应 (CPE) 是了解 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 致病性的关键,可用于评估体外病毒感染性。空斑测定基于病毒感染诱导的 CPE,为测试样本提供感染性病毒滴度。此外,该测定方法简单、定量且具有成本效益。因此,噬菌斑测定仍然是确定 CHIKV 感染性的金标准。然而,用肉眼或在显微镜下手动计数病毒诱导的斑块通常既耗时又费力。因此,自动噬菌斑计数软件将提高噬菌斑计数的一致性和效率。我们最近开发了 plaQuest,这是一款独立的 Windows 软件,可实现快速、可靠的 CHIKV 菌斑计数。在本章中,我们描述了在 24 孔板中检测和计数 CHIKV 形成的噬菌斑的基本程序。

papers.title: Impacto epidemiológico del dengue y del chikungunya en zonas urbanas: revisión sistemática Epidemiological impact of dengue and chikungunya in urban areas: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el impacto epidemiológico urbano del dengue y del chikungunya. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la incidencia mundial del dengue aumentó desde 1990, con diferencias regionales marcadas y alta carga en América Latina. El chikungunya se expandió por las Américas desde 2013 y produjo brotes urbanos explosivos, con manifestaciones articulares persistentes. La urbanización, la expansión de Aedes aegypti y Aedes albopictus y la resistencia a insecticidas favorecieron la transmisión. Destacan como estrategias las nuevas vacunas y el control vectorial integrado. Conclusión: ambas arbovirosis son una carga creciente para las ciudades tropicales y subtropicales y exigen vigilancia y control sostenidos.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review synthesizes the epidemiological impact of dengue and chikungunya in urban areas, focusing on the spread and burden of these diseases. The review included 15 studies from PubMed and SciELO between 2012 and 2025. Key findings indicate that dengue incidence has increased globally since 1990, with significant regional variations and a high burden in Latin America. Chikungunya expanded across the Americas since 2013, causing explosive urban outbreaks and persistent joint manifestations. Urbanization, the spread of Aedes species, and insecticide resistance are identified as factors that facilitate transmission. The review highlights the need for new vaccines and integrated vector control strategies to address the growing public health challenge posed by these arboviruses in tropical and subtropical cities.

papers.title: COINFECTION WITH PLASMODIUM VIVAX AND CHIKUNGUNYA; WHEN FEBRILE ILLNESS EVOLVES INTO HYPERDYNAMIC SHOCK: CASE REPORT
papers.abstract: Coinfection with malaria and chikungunya is a rare presentation and poses a diagnostic challenge., especially since both infections can produce systemic manifestations and hemodynamic compromise. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient from an urban area with no known past medical history, who presented with a seven-day history of fever, dizziness, generalized weakness, arthralgia, and vomiting. On admission, she was febrile, tachycardic, and hypotensive, with an insufficient hemodynamic response to initial resuscitation with crystalloids, requiring vasopressor support. Advanced cardiovascular evaluation revealed a predominantly vasodilatory and hyperdynamic profile, characterized by high cardiac output, decreased systemic vascular resistance, and preserved stroke volume. Left and right ventricular systolic and diastolic function remained preserved, with adequate TAPSE and MAPSE, and no significant chamber dilation or regional contractility abnormalities. The electrocardiogram and cardiac enzymes showed no evidence of myocardial injury or myocarditis. Studies revealed severe anemia, with a hemoglobin level of 6 g/ dL, and hepatosplenomegaly. Thick blood smear identified Plasmodium. The patient tested positive for vivax, while the PCR test for chikungunya was positive and the dengue test was negative, confirming the coinfection. Intravenous artesunate was initiated, followed by artemether-lumefantrine, in addition to vasoactive support and transfusion of two units of packed red blood cells. The patient experienced progressive hemodynamic recovery and a favorable clinical course. This case highlights the importance of considering vector-borne coinfections and characterizing the hemodynamic phenotype to differentiate vasodilatory shock from cardiogenic compromise.
papers.journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to highlight the diagnostic challenges posed by coinfection with Plasmodium vivax and Chikungunya virus, particularly in distinguishing their systemic manifestations and hemodynamic effects.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case report was conducted on a 23-year-old female patient from an urban area with no known past medical history, who presented with fever, dizziness, generalized weakness, arthralgia, and vomiting.
analysis.methods: The patient's coinfection was confirmed through PCR testing for Chikungunya virus and thick blood smear analysis for Plasmodium vivax, alongside clinical and hemodynamic evaluations.
analysis.main_results: Cardiovascular evaluation revealed a hyperdynamic profile with high cardiac output, decreased systemic vascular resistance, and preserved stroke volume, while no evidence of myocardial injury or myocarditis was found.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that coinfection with Plasmodium vivax and Chikungunya virus can lead to complex hemodynamic changes, necessitating careful differentiation from other causes of shock.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This case underscores the importance of recognizing vector-borne coinfections in febrile illnesses and emphasizes the need for accurate hemodynamic characterization in clinical settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single case report, which may not be generalizable. However, the evidence is strong given the detailed clinical and diagnostic findings.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 23-year-old female patient with coinfection of Plasmodium vivax and Chikungunya virus, presenting with fever, dizziness, generalized weakness, arthralgia, and vomiting. On admission, she exhibited hemodynamic instability, requiring vasopressor support. Cardiovascular evaluation revealed a hyperdynamic profile with high cardiac output and decreased systemic vascular resistance, but no evidence of myocardial injury or myocarditis. The study highlights the diagnostic challenges of coinfections and the importance of characterizing hemodynamic phenotypes to differentiate between vasodilatory shock and cardiogenic compromise. The case emphasizes the need for vigilance in identifying vector-borne coinfections in febrile illnesses. The evidence is strong due to the detailed clinical and diagnostic findings, though the study is limited to a single case report, which may affect generalizability.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 病例报告 对一名来自城市地区的 23 岁女性患者进行,该患者无既往病史,表现为发烧、头晕、全身无力、病例报告 和呕吐。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,间日疟原虫和 基孔肯雅病毒 的共同感染可导致复杂的血流动力学变化,需要与其他休克原因仔细区分。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该病例强调了在发热性疾病中识别 媒介 传播的合并感染的重要性,并强调了在临床环境中准确表征血流动力学特征的必要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单个病例报告,可能无法推广。然而,鉴于详细的临床和诊断结果,证据是强有力的。

papers.abstract_zh: 疟疾和基孔肯雅热的混合感染是一种罕见的表现,对诊断提出了挑战,特别是因为两种感染都会产生全身表现和血流动力学损害。我们介绍了一名来自城市地区的 23 岁女性患者,无既往病史,有 7 天发热、头晕、全身无力、关节痛 和呕吐病史。入院时,她出现发热、心动过速和低血压,对晶体液初始复苏的血流动力学反应不足,需要血管加压药支持。高级心血管评估显示主要是血管舒张和高动力特征,其特征是高心输出量、降低的全身血管阻力和保留的每搏输出量。左心室和右心室收缩和舒张功能仍然保留,具有足够的 TAPSE 和 MAPSE,并且没有明显的心室扩张或局部收缩力异常。心电图和心肌酶显示没有心肌损伤或心肌炎的证据。研究显示严重贫血,血红蛋白水平为 6 g/dL,并且肝脾肿大。厚厚的血涂片鉴定出疟原虫。该患者的间日疟检测呈阳性,而基孔肯雅热PCR检测呈阳性,登革热检测呈阴性,证实了双重感染。开始静脉注射青蒿琥酯,随后使用蒿甲醚-本芴醇,此外还进行血管活性支持和输注两个单位的浓缩红细胞。患者的血流动力学逐渐恢复,临床病程良好。该病例强调了考虑 媒介 传播的合并感染和表征血流动力学表型以区分血管舒张性休克和心源性损害的重要性。

papers.title: VIGILÂNCIA EPIDEMIOLÓGICA DAS ARBOVIROSES NO BRASIL: ESTRATÉGIAS ATUAIS PARA DENGUE, CHIKUNGUNYA, ZIKA E OROPOUCHE
papers.abstract: As arboviroses representam um dos principais desafios de saúde pública no Brasil, com epidemias recorrentes de dengue, circulação sustentada de chikungunya, impacto duradouro da epidemia de zika sobre a saúde materno-infantil e, mais recentemente, a reemergência e expansão geográfica do vírus Oropouche. Em 2024, o país registrou o maior número de casos prováveis de dengue de sua história, com milhões de notificações e milhares de óbitos, em um cenário favorecido pela urbanização desordenada, pelas falhas de saneamento e pelas mudanças climáticas. A vigilância epidemiológica das arboviroses envolve a notificação compulsória, a confirmação laboratorial, a vigilância entomológica, a análise oportuna dos dados para detecção de surtos e a integração com a assistência e o controle vetorial. Nos últimos anos, novas ferramentas ampliaram as possibilidades de vigilância e controle, como a vigilância genômica, que identificou uma linhagem rearranjada do vírus Oropouche associada à sua dispersão para além da Amazônia, os sistemas de alerta precoce baseados em dados climáticos, a liberação de mosquitos infectados com Wolbachia, que reduziu a incidência de dengue em ensaio randomizado e em estudo realizado em Niterói, e a vacinação contra dengue, incluindo a vacina de dose única desenvolvida pelo Instituto Butantan. Este capítulo revisa as características epidemiológicas das principais arboviroses no Brasil, as estratégias atuais de vigilância e controle e os desafios para a integração dessas ações ao SUS.

analysis.summary_en: This chapter addresses the public health challenge posed by arboviruses in Brazil, focusing on the epidemiological characteristics of chikungunya and other related arboviruses, current surveillance and control strategies, and the integration of these efforts within the SUS. The study highlights the recurring dengue outbreaks, sustained chikungunya circulation, long-term impact of the Zika epidemic on maternal and infant health, and the recent reemergence of Oropouche virus. It outlines the methods used in arbovirus surveillance, including mandatory notification, laboratory confirmation, entomological monitoring, and data analysis for outbreak detection. The main results emphasize the expansion of surveillance tools, such as genomic surveillance, climate-based early warning systems, Wolbachia-infected mosquito releases, and the single-dose dengue vaccine developed by Butantan. The authors interpret these findings as a review of current strategies and challenges in integrating them into the SUS. The scientific and public health significance lies in the potential to reduce arbovirus incidence and improve health system responses. The evidence is general and abstract, with no specific limitations or detailed assessments provided.

papers.title: Global Genomic Surveillance.
papers.abstract: Global genomic surveillance has emerged as a foundational pillar of public health in the twenty-first century, enabling real-time tracking of pathogen evolution and informing outbreak response. This chapter examines the strategic architecture of global genomic surveillance, focusing on its application to arboviruses such as chikungunya virus (CHIKV). It explores the integration of genomic data with epidemiological, clinical, and environmental information within a One Health framework, while addressing critical challenges in governance, equity, and interoperability. The discussion covers the entire genomic surveillance workflow, from sample collection and sequencing to bioinformatic analysis and phylogenetic inference, and highlights the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in predictive surveillance. By analyzing global initiatives, operational barriers, and emerging technologies, this chapter underscores the necessity of sustainable, equitable, and interoperable genomic systems to proactively address current and future infectious disease threats.

papers.title: Arthropod-Related Health Threats (ARHTs) and Nuisance Arthropods in North Khorasan Province, Iran: A Comprehensive Review.
papers.abstract: The arthropod vectors, such as mosquitoes, sand flies, and ticks, transmit various pathogens to humans and animals, leading to public health issues. Therefore, an effective disease surveillance system is essential to provide information on these diseases in order to monitor their trends worldwide. The current study focused on the prevalence of arthropod-borne diseases and their vectors in North Khorasan Province located in northeastern Iran, bordering Turkmenistan. A narrative literature review was conducted to analyze the status of arthropod-related health threats (ARHTs) and their vectors in this area. Sources with no time limit up to 2025 were examined from PubMed, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science databases using keywords like vector, arthropod, North Khorasan, and Iran. After excluding duplicates and irrelevant content, a final list of 31 papers was thoroughly evaluated. This province exhibits the occurrence of several major ARHTs, including visceral leishmaniasis, cutaneous leishmaniasis, West Nile fever, chikungunya, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, Q fever, Theileria infection, equine piroplasmosis, dirofilariasis, Dipylidium caninum infection, fascioliasis, hymenolepiasis, scorpionism, spider bites, pediculosis, and myiasis. Given the complex and diverse ecosystem of North Khorasan, implementing tailored and innovative strategies is essential for effective surveillance and early detection of arthropod-borne diseases, thus enabling timely and efficient management of these health threats.

elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该评论指出了北呼罗珊地区生态系统的复杂性和多样性,这可能会影响疾病 传播 的动态。然而,它没有提供关于监测策略的比较有效性或基孔肯雅病毒 传播的详细机制的具体证据。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines the role of arthropod vectors in transmitting pathogens, including chikungunya virus, to humans and animals, leading to public health issues. The central question is the prevalence and impact of arthropod-borne diseases in North Khorasan Province, Iran.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science databases, with sources up to 2025. Keywords included vector, arthropod, North Khorasan, and Iran. After excluding duplicates and irrelevant content, 31 papers were thoroughly evaluated.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study identifies chikungunya virus as one of the major arthropod-borne pathogens in North Khorasan Province, alongside other diseases. It highlights the need for effective surveillance systems to monitor these diseases globally.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes the complexity and diversity of the ecosystem in North Khorasan, which may affect disease transmission dynamics. However, it does not provide specific evidence on the comparative effectiveness of surveillance strategies or detailed mechanisms of chikungunya virus transmission.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Implementing tailored and innovative strategies is essential for effective surveillance and early detection of arthropod-borne diseases, including chikungunya virus, to enable timely and efficient management of these health threats.

papers.title_zh: 伊朗北呼罗珊省节肢动物相关健康威胁 (ARHT) 和滋扰节肢动物:全面审查。
papers.source_body_en: The arthropod vectors, such as mosquitoes, sand flies, and ticks, transmit various pathogens to humans and animals, leading to public health issues. Therefore, an effective disease surveillance system is essential to provide information on these diseases in order to monitor their trends worldwide. The current study focused on the prevalence of arthropod-borne diseases and their vectors in North Khorasan Province located in northeastern Iran, bordering Turkmenistan. A narrative literature review was conducted to analyze the status of arthropod-related health threats (ARHTs) and their vectors in this area. Sources with no time limit up to 2025 were examined from PubMed, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science databases using keywords like vector, arthropod, North Khorasan, and Iran. After excluding duplicates and irrelevant content, a final list of 31 papers was thoroughly evaluated. This province exhibits the occurrence of several major ARHTs, including visceral leishmaniasis, cutaneous leishmaniasis, West Nile fever, chikungunya, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, Q fever, Theileria infection, equine piroplasmosis, dirofilariasis, Dipylidium caninum infection, fascioliasis, hymenolepiasis, scorpionism, spider bites, pediculosis, and myiasis. Given the complex and diverse ecosystem of North Khorasan, implementing tailored and innovative strategies is essential for effective surveillance and early detection of arthropod-borne diseases, thus enabling timely and efficient management of these health threats.

papers.title: Solanaceae-Derived Spirostane Saponins Inhibit Dengue Virus Replication and Viral Protein Expression and Exhibit Activity Against Multiple Arboviruses.
papers.abstract: Mosquito-borne arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), represent a growing global health burden, yet no specific antiviral therapies are currently available for most of these infections. This unmet need highlights the importance of identifying novel antiviral compounds from biologically relevant sources such as plant-derived natural products. In this study, a bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells. Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Subsequent fractionation and purification led to the isolation of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, structurally characterized by UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy. Functional assays demonstrated that these compounds inhibit DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. Stage-specific analyses revealed that their antiviral activity is primarily associated with intracellular phases of the viral life cycle, consistent with inhibition of viral replication and/or protein processing. Molecular docking analyses supported these findings by predicting favorable interactions with key viral enzymes, particularly NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and NS3 helicase/protease. Importantly, the isolated compounds retained antiviral activity against ZIKV and CHIKV, indicating cross-arboviral efficacy. Together, these findings identify spirostane saponins as promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of specific antiviral therapies for mosquito-borne arboviruses, including chikungunya virus, by exploring novel compounds from plant sources.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a bioactivity-guided approach to screen methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species for antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells, with a focus on chikungunya virus.
analysis.methods: The researchers used bioactivity-guided screening, fractionation, and purification techniques to isolate compounds, followed by structural characterization using UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy, and functional assays to assess antiviral activity.
analysis.main_results: Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Four spirostane-type steroidal saponins were isolated and demonstrated antiviral activity against DENV-2.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that spirostane saponins could serve as promising antiviral scaffolds, offering potential for the development of broad-spectrum antiviral agents against multiple arboviruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for further research into plant-derived compounds as therapeutic options for chikungunya virus and other related arboviruses, potentially contributing to surveillance and treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro findings and does not address in vivo efficacy or clinical translation, which reduces the strength of the evidence to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the potential of Solanaceae-derived spirostane saponins as antiviral agents against chikungunya virus and other arboviruses. The research highlights the growing global health burden of mosquito-borne viruses, including chikungunya, and the lack of specific therapies. A bioactivity-guided approach was used to screen extracts from eight Solanaceae species, identifying compounds that inhibit DENV-2 replication in Vero cells. Structural characterization and functional assays confirmed the antiviral activity of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, with evidence suggesting their efficacy against multiple arboviruses. The findings indicate that these compounds could be promising scaffolds for developing broad-spectrum antiviral agents. However, the study is limited to in vitro results, which restricts the strength of the evidence to moderate. The results may inform future research into plant-derived therapies for chikungunya and related viruses, contributing to surveillance and treatment strategies.

elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用生物活性引导的筛选、分馏和纯化技术来分离化合物,然后使用 UPLC-DAD-MS 和 1D/2D NMR 光谱进行结构表征,并进行功能测定以评估 抗病毒药物 活性。
elements_zh.main_results: 五种提取物显着降低了病毒感染性,其中包括 Solanum ovalifolium 和 Cestrum sp。在非细胞毒性浓度下实现完全抑制。分离出四种螺罗坦型甾体皂苷,并证明了 抗病毒药物 对抗 DENV-2 的活性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,螺罗坦皂苷可以作为有前途的 抗病毒药物 支架,为开发针对多种虫媒病毒的广谱 抗病毒药物 药物提供了潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该结果为进一步研究植物源化合物作为 基孔肯雅病毒 和其他相关虫媒病毒的治疗选择奠定了基础,可能有助于 监测 和 治疗 策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外研究结果,不涉及体内疗效或临床转化,这将证据的强度降至中等。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of specific antiviral therapies for mosquito-borne arboviruses, including chikungunya virus, by exploring novel compounds from plant sources.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study employed a bioactivity-guided approach to screen methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species for antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells, with a focus on chikungunya virus.
analysis_en.methods: The researchers used bioactivity-guided screening, fractionation, and purification techniques to isolate compounds, followed by structural characterization using UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy, and functional assays to assess antiviral activity.
analysis_en.main_results: Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Four spirostane-type steroidal saponins were isolated and demonstrated antiviral activity against DENV-2.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that spirostane saponins could serve as promising antiviral scaffolds, offering potential for the development of broad-spectrum antiviral agents against multiple arboviruses.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for further research into plant-derived compounds as therapeutic options for chikungunya virus and other related arboviruses, potentially contributing to surveillance and treatment strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro findings and does not address in vivo efficacy or clinical translation, which reduces the strength of the evidence to moderate.

papers.title_zh: 来自茄科植物的螺甾烷皂苷抑制登革病毒复制和病毒蛋白表达,并对多种虫媒病毒具有活性。
papers.source_body_en: Mosquito-borne arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), represent a growing global health burden, yet no specific antiviral therapies are currently available for most of these infections. This unmet need highlights the importance of identifying novel antiviral compounds from biologically relevant sources such as plant-derived natural products. In this study, a bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells. Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Subsequent fractionation and purification led to the isolation of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, structurally characterized by UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy. Functional assays demonstrated that these compounds inhibit DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. Stage-specific analyses revealed that their antiviral activity is primarily associated with intracellular phases of the viral life cycle, consistent with inhibition of viral replication and/or protein processing. Molecular docking analyses supported these findings by predicting favorable interactions with key viral enzymes, particularly NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and NS3 helicase/protease. Importantly, the isolated compounds retained antiviral activity against ZIKV and CHIKV, indicating cross-arboviral efficacy. Together, these findings identify spirostane saponins as promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.
papers.abstract_zh: 由蚊子传播的虫媒病毒,包括登革病毒(DENV)、寨卡病毒(ZIKV)和基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV),构成了日益增长的全球健康负担,但目前针对这些感染的特定抗病毒药物疗法尚不普及。这种未满足的需求凸显了从生物相关来源(如植物来源的天然产物)中识别新型抗病毒药物化合物的重要性。本研究采用生物活性引导的方法,对八种茄科植物的甲醇提取物进行筛选,以鉴定具有抗病毒药物活性的化合物,针对Vero细胞中的DENV-2。五种提取物显著降低了病毒感染性,其中Solanum ovalifolium和Cestrum sp.在非细胞毒性浓度下实现了完全抑制。随后的分级和纯化过程分离出四种螺甾烷型甾体皂苷,其结构通过UPLC-DAD-MS和1D/2D NMR光谱法进行了表征。功能实验表明,这些化合物抑制了DENV的复制,表现为病毒RNA水平的显著降低、NS1和NS3蛋白表达的减少以及传染性病毒滴度的下降。阶段特异性分析显示,其抗病毒药物活性主要与病毒生命周期的细胞内阶段相关,这与抑制病毒复制和/或蛋白加工一致。分子对接分析支持了这些发现,预测了这些化合物与关键病毒酶的有利相互作用,特别是NS5 RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶和NS3解旋酶/蛋白酶。重要的是,分离出的化合物对ZIKV和CHIKV也表现出抗病毒药物活性,表明其对多种虫媒病毒具有交叉疗效。综上所述,这些发现将螺甾烷皂苷识别为有前景的抗病毒药物骨架,并支持其进一步开发为广谱抗病毒药物药物。

papers.title: Rainfall and human activities drive Aedes aegypti breeding sites infestation and larval density in urban and rural settings of Bobo-Dioulasso in western Burkina Faso
papers.abstract: Aedes aegypti , the primary vector of dengue, chikungunya and Zika, breeds mainly in artificial containers around households, and its larval abundance reflects a complex interplay between climate and human practices. In our cross-sectional survey conducted in urban and rural sectors of Bobo-Dioulasso across dry and rainy seasons, entomological indices exceeded WHO epidemic thresholds, with the House Index reaching 66.7% and the Breteau Index ranging from 107 to 147, indicating sustained transmission risk. Infestation varied markedly by container type. Domestic materials (41.9%), basins (29.4%) and flower pots (28.6%) showed the highest positivity rates, whereas kettles and animal skins were rarely colonized. Notably, although less frequent, terracotta jars, barrels, tires and miscellaneous containers produced more than 70% of all larvae, identifying them as principal production sites. This confirms that structural characteristics of containers, rather than their abundance alone, decisively shape larval habitat suitability. Seasonality also structured larval dynamics. More containers were positive during the dry season, but mean density was three-fold higher in the rainy season, with rainfall exhibiting a non-linear relationship, intermediate precipitation promoting proliferation. After accounting for climatic variables, urban households consistently harbored higher larval densities, reflecting intensive water storage and inadequate waste management. Collectively, proliferation is driven by the combined effects of rainfall dynamics and human practices. Container-related structural and ecological factors, type, exposure and organic matter, therefore exert a more pronounced influence on larval productivity than mere container availability. Interventions should prioritize highly productive containers, particularly jars, barrels and tires, by integrating rainfall-based surveillance with community-led source reduction in areas at greatest transmission risk.
